solution_text.en:
"…the requirement is expected to swell from 72 million tonnes to 236 million tonnes."

The figure rises from 72 to 236, so swell here means to grow larger (बढ़ना, फूलना).

Why the others are wrong.

• Dwindle = to become gradually smaller (घटते जाना): opposite meaning — the trap.

• Dwell = to live in a place, or to keep thinking about something (निवास करना; किसी बात पर देर तक सोचना): sound-alike of swell, unrelated meaning.

• Fluctuate = to rise and fall again and again (उतार-चढ़ाव होना): same field (change in amount), but not the same meaning. The figure goes only one way, from 72 to 236.

Answer: Increase

Word help.

• requirement (आवश्यकता)

• yardstick (मानदंड, मापदंड)

When a vocabulary word sits next to numbers, let the numbers decide the meaning.

solution_text.en:
The author welcomes the ambition:

"…the draft… is nothing if not ambitious… a welcome admission that a two-decade forecast is a compass rather than a contract."

But the author questions the method:

"Yet the document carries a contradiction at its core." and "The sensible response is not to scale back the ambition but to change the yardstick."

So the goal is backed, the route is criticised.

Why the others are wrong.

• Admiring and largely uncritical: the author points out a contradiction, questions incentives and warns against tariff walls.

• Sceptical of the target and dismissive of the whole plan: the author explicitly does not want to "scale back the ambition".

• Alarmed and pessimistic: the tone is calm and offers solutions (scrap, renewables, hydrogen); it is not alarmist.

Answer: Supportive of the goal but critical of the chosen path

Word help.

• safeguards (सुरक्षा उपाय)

• tariff wall (ऊँचे आयात शुल्क की दीवार)

• incentives (प्रोत्साहन)

'Not to scale back the ambition but to change the yardstick' = support the aim, fix the method.

option_1.en: The doctor advised the patient that he did not climb the stairs for a week.

option_2.en: The doctor advised the patient do not climb the stairs for a week.

option_3.en: The doctor forbade the patient not to climb the stairs for a week.

option_4.en: The doctor advised the patient not to climb the stairs for a week.

question.en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

The doctor said to the patient, "Do not climb the stairs for a week."

solution_text.en:
Rule: A negative command (Do not / Don't + verb) is reported as told / advised / ordered + object + not + to-infinitive. Another way is forbade + object + to-infinitive: 'forbade' already carries the 'not', so no second 'not' is added.

Example: He said to me, "Don't go there." → He told me not to go there. / He forbade me to go there.

(निषेधात्मक आज्ञा का अप्रत्यक्ष कथन)

Apply it.

• said to → advised (a doctor's instruction is advice)

• Do not climb → not to climb

• 'for a week' stays as it is (no time word to change)

→ The doctor advised the patient not to climb the stairs for a week.

Why the others are wrong.

• that he did not climb: a command is not reported with a that-clause; it needs the to-infinitive.

• do not climb: the imperative form is kept; it must become not to climb.

• forbade… not to climb: 'forbade' is already negative, so 'not' makes it a double negative. Correct form: forbade the patient to climb.

Answer: The doctor advised the patient not to climb the stairs for a week.

Don't + verb → not + to + verb. With 'forbade', drop the 'not'.

question.en:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.

The list of candidates shortlisted / for the final round of interviews / have been displayed / on the notice board.

solution_text.en:
Rule: When a phrase comes between the subject and the verb, the verb agrees with the head noun of the subject, not with the noun nearest to it.

Example: The colour of the flowers is bright. (head noun: colour)

(कर्ता का मुख्य संज्ञा शब्द क्रिया तय करता है)

Apply it.

• Subject: The list (singular)

• 'of candidates shortlisted for the final round of interviews' only describes the list.

• Verb must be singular → has been displayed

→ The list of candidates shortlisted for the final round of interviews has been displayed on the notice board.

Why the others are fine.

• The list of candidates shortlisted: correct; 'shortlisted' after the noun is a normal participle phrase.

• for the final round of interviews: correct preposition and article.

• on the notice board: correct preposition.

Answer: have been displayed

Cover the 'of…' phrase with your finger: 'The list… has been displayed.'

question.en:
Four of the following five sentences form a coherent paragraph. Identify the sentence that does NOT belong to it.

A. Honeybees pollinate a large share of the crops that farmers grow for food.

B. In recent years, however, bee colonies in many regions have been shrinking.

C. Scientists link the decline to pesticides, the loss of wild flowers and disease.

D. Honey has been valued as a medicine since ancient times.

E. Some farmers have now begun planting strips of wild flowers to give the bees a safer home.

solution_text.en:
Find the thread.

The paragraph is about bees as pollinators, their decline, and what is being done about it.

• A: why bees matter (pollination of crops)

• B: "however": the problem, colonies are shrinking

• C: "the decline": causes of the problem in B

• E: a response: wild-flower strips, which answers "loss of wild flowers" in C

The odd one.

D talks about honey as a medicine in ancient times. It mentions a bee product, but it has nothing to do with pollination, the decline or its remedy. It breaks the chain.

Answer: D

The paragraph.

Honeybees pollinate a large share of the crops that farmers grow for food. In recent years, however, bee colonies in many regions have been shrinking. Scientists link the decline to pesticides, the loss of wild flowers and disease. Some farmers have now begun planting strips of wild flowers to give the bees a safer home.

The odd sentence often shares the topic word (bees, honey) but not the thread.

Word help: pollinate (परागण करना), colony (मधुमक्खियों का छत्ता/समूह)

question.en:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the underlined part of the given sentence.

The committee decided to repair the old hall rather than building a new one.

solution_text.en:
Rule: Items joined by as well as or rather than must be in the same grammatical form (parallel). If the first item is a to-infinitive, the second is a bare infinitive (or to-infinitive); if the first is a gerund, the second is a gerund.

Example: She chose to walk rather than take the bus. / She enjoys reading as well as writing.

(समानांतर संरचना)

Apply it.

First item: decided to repair (infinitive)

So the second item must also be an infinitive: (to) build.

→ The committee decided to repair the old hall rather than build a new one.

Why the others are wrong.

• built: past form; does not match 'to repair'.

• having built: perfect participle; wrong form and wrong time (the hall is not yet built).

• to building: 'to' + -ing is not an infinitive here; rather than to building is ungrammatical.

Answer: build

Look at the verb form BEFORE 'rather than' and copy it after.

option_1.en: The old temple wall were rebuilt by the villagers within a week.

option_2.en: The old temple wall has been rebuilt by the villagers within a week.

option_3.en: The old temple wall was rebuilt by the villagers within a week.

option_4.en: The old temple wall is rebuilt by the villagers within a week.

question.en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The villagers rebuilt the old temple wall within a week.

solution_text.en:
Rule: Simple past active (V2) → passive was/were + V3. The object becomes the new subject, and the auxiliary must agree with that new subject: singular → was, plural → were.

Example: The police caught the thieves. → The thieves were caught by the police.

(सामान्य भूतकाल कर्मवाच्य)

Apply it.

• Verb: rebuilt (simple past)

• New subject: the old temple wall (singular) → was

• V3 of rebuild → rebuilt

→ The old temple wall was rebuilt by the villagers within a week.

Why the others are wrong.

• were rebuilt: 'were' agrees with the old subject villagers, not with the new subject wall.

• has been rebuilt: present perfect passive; the tense has changed.

• is rebuilt: simple present passive; the tense has changed.

Answer: The old temple wall was rebuilt by the villagers within a week.

In the passive, look at the NEW subject before choosing was or were.

question.en: Select the correctly spelt word.

solution_text.en:
Meaning: jeopardy = danger of loss, harm or failure (ख़तरा, जोखिम)

Example: The floods put the whole harvest in jeopardy.

Spelling build-up.

jeo + par + dy → Jeopardy

The silent o follows 'je' (as in leopard), and the middle syllable is -par- with an 'a'.

Why the others are wrong.

• Jeapordy: 'o' and 'a' swapped – 'jea-por' instead of 'jeo-par'.

• Jepardy: the silent 'o' is dropped.

• Jeoperdy: 'a' wrongly changed to 'e' in the middle syllable.

Jeopardy is spelt like leopard: le-o-pard → je-o-pard-y.

question.en:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no improvement is required, select 'No improvement'.

It takes the goods train nearly four minutes to pass across the long tunnel cut into the hillside.

solution_text.en:
Rule: Across = from one side to the other of a surface (across a road, across a field, across a river). Through = from one end to the other inside something enclosed (through a tunnel, through a forest, through a crowd).

Example: We walked across the bridge, then the road ran through a dense forest.

(across = सतह के आर-पार; through = किसी चीज़ के भीतर से होकर)

Apply it.

A tunnel is an enclosed passage. The train enters at one end and comes out at the other, moving inside it. So the train passes through the tunnel, not across it. The four minutes also show it is travelling the length of the tunnel.

→ It takes the goods train nearly four minutes to pass through the long tunnel cut into the hillside.

Why the others are wrong.

• pass beside: means going alongside the tunnel (बगल से), which a train cannot do with a tunnel cut into a hillside.

• pass over: means going above it (ऊपर से); the train runs inside, not on top.

• No improvement: 'across' suits a surface, not an enclosed passage.

Answer: pass through

Surface → across; inside something → through.

question.en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

Is the final draft checked by the two editors before it goes to print?

solution_text.en:
Rule: Simple present passive is is/am/are + V3. In the active, the agent after 'by' becomes the subject, the passive subject becomes the object, and the verb returns to the simple present. In a question, the helping verb is do/does + V1, and it must agree with the new subject.

Example: Is the letter written by her? → Does she write the letter?

(सामान्य वर्तमान काल; प्रश्नवाचक कर्तृवाच्य)

Apply it.

• Agent: the two editors → new subject (plural)

• Plural subject → Do (not Does)

• Main verb after do → base form check

• Object: the final draft

→ Do the two editors check the final draft before it goes to print?

Why the others are wrong.

• Does the two editors: 'Does' agrees with the old singular subject draft; the new subject editors is plural.

• Are… checking: present continuous; the tense has changed.

• Do… checked: after do/does the verb must be V1, not V3.

Answer: Do the two editors check the final draft before it goes to print?

The 'Is' of the passive does not decide Do/Does: the new subject does.
